about: One row per kind of lawmaking body (engine map line 28, E3: one bill engine, the level a row). The bill and budget engine (src/core2/modules/legislature.ts) reads a body's level, the legislature its chambers belong to, the chamber a bill or budget starts in, the words for the body, and who holds the veto, from these rows instead of branching on the office kind. `kindPrefix` matches an office kind (us-house also covers the delegate and at-large rows). A body with no `legislature` is a one-chamber body. `chamberId` is the nation's own id for a federal chamber, which has one office row per state. Structure is law (U.S. Const. art. I; state constitutions; county and municipal codes); each row cites it.

bodies.source: U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 1 and 7: Congress is a House and a Senate; revenue bills originate in the House.
U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 1 and 3.
Each state constitution's legislative article; Nebraska's one chamber is the one legislature- row its state has.
State county codes: the county's governing board adopts its budget (src/core2/gov-rules/county-governing-body-rules.ts).
Municipal charters and codes: the council is the municipal legislative body (src/core2/data/offices/body-names.json).
State township codes: where the town's own government is its township, the township board is its legislative body.

vetoHolder.source: U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 7 (the president's veto); state constitutions (the governor's); county and municipal charters (the county executive's and the mayor's, where the office exists).
